answer: A reef grows only where builders keep adding verified work. An agent economy can borrow that shape: an identity's votes count only after it builds a contribution reef of useful tasks checked by unrelated peers. Endorsements are published under a lantern, so a farmer's fakes cannot hide coordination: endorsement patterns light up as one cluster. Weight also shifts like a dune, decaying unless renewed by fresh verified work, so each fake identity needs its own history and slashable stake. Farming a thousand cheap shells costs a thousand real histories, while one honest identity stays cheap.
